# Workspace images

Workspace images let the jobs that install the dependencies start from a disk image of a workspace of `main` instead of an empty folder: the test jobs of pull requests ([pr-linux-test.yml](../pr-linux-test.yml) and [pr-win32-test.yml](../pr-win32-test.yml)), the Compile & Hygiene, Monaco Editor, Copilot test and chat-lib test jobs of [pr.yml](../pr.yml), and the Playwright Fixture Tests and Screenshots jobs of [component-fixtures.yml](../component-fixtures.yml), also on pushes. Its dependencies, Electron and the Playwright browsers are installed, and its `.git` holds the commit it was built at. A job mounts the image, checks out its own commit, and installs only what changed since, which for most pull requests is nothing.

The Windows and Linux jobs that install the dependencies use the images, except the Windows WSL smoke test job (`Windows / Electron-Smoke (WSL)`), which runs on the 1ES pool and keeps its workspace on drive C: WSL cannot open folders on a volume that is mounted in a folder of drive C:. A job can only use an image on runners whose workspaces have the path of the workspace of the image: those that build it (`vscode-large-runners-ubuntu-8-core` and `vscode-large-runners-windows-8-core`), and the dedicated runners of the merge queue and of the pull requests to release branches, which have the same image and size (`vscode-large-runners-ubuntu-8-core-merge-queue` and `vscode-large-runners-windows-8-core-merge-queue`, see [pr.yml](../pr.yml)). The merge queue uses the images of `main`. The other jobs of `pr.yml` don't install the dependencies of the workspace, so an image would only add its download: Detect Changes, Telemetry, Copilot - Check Telemetry, Ripple, the Rust jobs of [pr-linux-cli-test.yml](../pr-linux-cli-test.yml), Cancel Run and PR Gate. The macOS test jobs never adopted them, and are commented out in [pr.yml](../pr.yml) for now, like the job of [pr-workspace-images.yml](../pr-workspace-images.yml) that builds the macOS image. [What a job does](#what-a-job-does) describes the steps of a job that uses the images.

[pr-workspace-images.yml](../pr-workspace-images.yml) builds an image for Linux and Windows on the runners of the jobs every day at 05:00 UTC, and when one of its inputs changes on `main`: those of the install, of the native builds (`NATIVE_BUILD_INPUTS` in `image.ts`) and of the prepared Electron. It doesn't build them for other pushes, as the checkout of a job fetches and writes only what changed since the commit of its image. The images are kept for 2 days, so the daily build keeps a recent image available. [image.ts](image.ts) restores, checks and builds them; it has no dependencies, as the jobs run it before they check out the repository.

## What a job does

1. **Downloads the scripts** of its commit from the API (`image.ts`, and on Windows `win32/vhd.ps1` and `win32/Vhd.cs`), and `.nvmrc` for the Node.js version.
2. **Restores the image** (`image.ts restore`): finds the newest image of `main`, downloads it with parallel range requests, and mounts it at the parent folder of the workspace, so that the workspace keeps its path. Without an image, or on any error, it warns and the job installs everything: the test jobs with the cached pnpm store as before, and the jobs of `pr.yml` and `component-fixtures.yml` without it. It gives up after 4 minutes (`--timeout-seconds`), before the timeout of its step could stop it with the image half attached, and then, as after any other error, unmounts and detaches the image, so that the workspace is an empty folder again; on Windows, it also deletes the VHDX, whose data Windows keeps in memory. Pull requests to release branches look for images of their own branch (`--branch`), which aren't built, and install everything as before, like the jobs of `component-fixtures.yml` on pushes to release branches. The job also doesn't use an image when the inputs of the base key of a `node_modules` folder (`computeNodeModulesBaseCacheKey` in `build/azure-pipelines/common/cacheKeys.ts`: the salt of the CI caches, the pnpmfiles, the `nativeBuild` targets and `packageManager` of `package.json`, the Node.js versions and the pnpm settings of the install roots, mirrored in `NATIVE_BUILD_INPUTS` of `image.ts`) differ between the commit of the image and its own, which the restore compares through the API before it downloads anything: installing on top of an image wouldn't build its native modules again, for example after an Electron update.
3. **Checks out its commit** with `clean: false`, which keeps the untracked files of the image and reuses its checkout: the shallow fetch sends the tag at the commit of the image, and downloads only what changed since, and git writes only the files that changed, as it compares their sizes and modification times, which the image keeps.
4. **Installs the dependencies** with its usual install steps, on the `node_modules` of the image instead of an empty folder, and with the pnpm store of the image instead of the cached store (see [CI caches](../caches/README.md)). `pnpm install`, whose postinstall installs every other install root, installs only what changed since the commit of the image, as pnpm checks itself what is up to date. The Copilot and chat-lib jobs install only the projects of the root workspace that they need, without the root install scripts, which the image installed with the rest of the workspace. On Linux, `setup-env.sh` reuses the sysroots and compilers in the `.build` folder of the image, and the system packages are installed as before, as they aren't in the image. On Windows, the jobs set `GODEBUG=winreadlinkvolume=1`, so that esbuild resolves pnpm's junctions on the image, which is mounted without a drive letter.
5. **Keeps the prepared Electron** when it was prepared from the same inputs (see [setup-electron](../../actions/setup-electron/action.yml)), and finds the Playwright browsers in the image (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`), instead of in their cache, which would point `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` into the workspace.

## The images

The workspace of an image is at the path of the workspaces of the jobs, because pnpm links packages of different folders with junctions on Windows, whose targets are absolute paths, and records its store in `node_modules/.modules.yaml`: with another store, pnpm installs every package again. The store (`pnpm_config_store_dir`) and the Playwright browsers are beside the workspace, in the image. The jobs don't need the content of the store: with an empty store at the same path, pnpm only downloads the packages that changed. On Windows, pnpm hard links the packages from the store, as its clones on ReFS store them again.

| Platform | Image | Restore |
| -------- | ----- | ------- |
| Linux | ext4 volume without a journal in a sparse file | Attached to a loop device while still empty, recreated from chunks of zstd, then mounted with `barrier=0`, while the kernel writes the image to the disk |
| macOS | APFS volume in a sparse ASIF image | Recreated from chunks of zstd, then attached |
| Windows | Dev Drive in a VHDX with blocks of 1 MB | Recreated from chunks of zstd into a temporary file, which Windows keeps in memory, then attached through the file system cache with the virtual disk API ([Vhd.cs](win32/Vhd.cs)) |

All three are writable volumes. A squashfs under an overlay, which Linux mounts without writing it, took seconds to look up the files of a checkout or `node_modules` for the first time, as squashfs reads its metadata past the caches of the kernel.

The chunks of 32 MB download and decompress in parallel, and the restore writes them in order as they arrive, without the pages of zeros where the file can be sparse. On Windows, the disk sets the pace, at 250-650 MB/s, as a VHDX can be neither sparse nor written later. The first PowerShell of a job takes seconds to start, so [vhd.ps1](win32/vhd.ps1) starts and compiles the virtual disk API while the image downloads into the file that `image.ts` created. On Linux, attaching a file to a loop device waits for the kernel to write the file to the disk, so the restore attaches the empty file while the image downloads, and drops what udev read from it before it mounts the volume. With `barrier=0`, an fsync in the volume doesn't wait for the rest of the image to reach the disk either. Images keep everything of the workspace: the checkout of their commit with HEAD detached (`image.ts seed`), the files that pnpm installed, and the `.build` folder (Electron, and on Linux the sysroots and compilers of `setup-env.sh`).

## Trust

A job only uses images of runs of this repository for pushes to `main`, its daily schedule and manual dispatches, as any pull request could upload an artifact of the same name. The `.git` of an image holds no credentials. The jobs that use the images need `actions: read` to find and download the artifacts.

## Testing changes

`pr-workspace-images.yml` can be called with `workflow_call`, so that a temporary workflow on a branch can build the images of the branch, and test the steps of a job that restores them with `image.ts restore --branch`.

## Azure Pipelines

The Linux, macOS and Windows CI test jobs of the product build (`build/azure-pipelines/product-build.yml`) use workspace images too, in the pipeline cache instead of artifacts, with the packed format and the mounts of `image.ts`: [workspaceImage.ts](../../../build/azure-pipelines/common/workspaceImage.ts) and [workspace-image.yml](../../../build/azure-pipelines/common/workspace-image.yml). The product builds don't use them yet.

- **The image** is the sources directory of a Linux, macOS or Windows job after the install steps of `product-build-linux-setup.yml`, `product-build-darwin-setup.yml` or `product-build-win32-setup.yml`, with its own pnpm store in `.build/pnpm-store`. The image job installs without the distro and the other private repositories, so an image holds neither their sources nor their credentials: the test jobs check them out, and install the distro roots on top of the image.
- **The cache key** is the base key of `node_modules` folders (`computeNodeModulesBaseCacheKey`, without the distro roots), then a key of the lockfiles of every install root and of the day the pipeline run started. A new image is built after a change to the lockfiles, on the first CI build of a day, and with new native build inputs; there can be several images of one day.
- **The image job** of the stage (`Linux (X64) - Image`, `macOS (ARM64) - Image`, `Windows (X64) - Image`) looks the current key up. When the cache doesn't have it, the job mounts an empty volume over its checkout, runs the setup steps of the test jobs in it, and packs it into the folder that the cache saves at the end of the job. The cache saves only after a job that fully succeeded, and the job continues on error, so its failures don't fail the build.
- **The test jobs** don't wait for it. Right after their checkout, they restore the current key, or the newest image of the same native build inputs, mount it over the checkout, bring its checkout to the commit of the job from the checkout of the job, and install on top of it. Without an image, or on any error, they unmount it, which leaves the checkout of the job, and install everything as before.
- **Only the image job saves images.** The cache task has no restore-only mode: it saves its folder at the end of every job that succeeded without restoring its key exactly, unless the key was saved meanwhile. So a test job that didn't restore the current image exactly changes its key to one that no image has, and empties the folder, before the end of the job.
- **On macOS**, the agents run macOS 15, which has no ASIF images or `diskutil image`, so the volume is an APFS volume in a sparse image (`.sparseimage`) that `hdiutil` attaches over the checkout, like the ext4 volume on Linux. It is attached out of Finder and with `-owners off`, so that the jobs can read the folders that macOS keeps at the root of a volume, such as `.fseventsd`. `.metadata_never_index` and `.fseventsd/no_log` at its root keep Spotlight and fseventsd away from it, and `.git/info/exclude` keeps them out of git. The image job detaches the volume, which leaves its own checkout in the sources directory, and compacts the sparse image before packing it.
- **On Windows**, the agents run Windows Server 2022, which has no Dev Drives, so an image is an NTFS volume in a VHDX (`vhd.ps1 -Create -FileSystem NTFS`), which the test jobs restore and attach like the jobs of pull requests. A volume can only be mounted at an empty folder, so a job moves its checkout into the temporary folder of the agent, on the same disk, while the volume is mounted at the sources directory, and moves it back when it unmounts the volume: the test jobs after an error, the image job after it detached the volume to pack it. The volume is mounted at the sources directory, not at its parent folder, which holds files of the 1ES steps, so the jobs delete `System Volume Information`, which Windows creates at the root of a volume when the image job gives it a drive letter, and which the scripts that walk the repository can't read. The jobs that start from an image set `GODEBUG=winreadlinkvolume=1`, and after the install steps, they replace pnpm's relative links that go up to the root of the image, such as `extensions/npm/node_modules/which`, with junctions: esbuild drops the separator after the volume name when it follows a link up to the root of a volume without a drive letter, which the GitHub images avoid, as their links go up to the workspace folder at most. The Windows smoke test job (`Smoke Tests (Electron)`) doesn't use one, like the WSL smoke test job of pull requests.
